speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for sharing that. To begin our assessment, have you experienced any fever, abdominal pain, or blood in your stool recently?

REQUEST TEST: CBC (Complete Blood Count) and CMP (Comprehensive Metabolic Panel)

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: Hemoglobin 13 g/dL, Total Count WBC 13,400/mm3, Differential Count Neutrophils 80%, Lymphocytes 15%, Monocytes 5%. Comprehensive Metabolic Panel: NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Currently being treated for community-acquired pneumonia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol. No recent travel or dietary changes reported.

speaker: Patient
text: No fever, no recent antibiotics usage apart from levofloxacin for pneumonia, no vomiting, no blood in stool. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is interesting; could you confirm if the "diarrhea" you experienced was actually urine leakage or a sensation of urgency, given the UTI diagnosis? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis and Urine Culture to verify the UTI and rule out other causes. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Urinary Tract Infection (UTI) with possible misinterpretation of symptoms as diarrhea.
